title: Investigation of concrete durability enhancement using supplementary cementitious materials
author: S, Rajagopal, et al.
materials: This dual-stage pozzolanic reaction enhances both early and long-term strength and durability. Thermodynamically, the Gibbs free energy for C-S-H formation from both materials is negative (∆G < 0), but metakaolin achieves equilibrium faster, accelerating the reduction of CH and improving pore structure.

steps.title: Extract P. juliflora material
steps.instruction: Obtain 600 g of finely powdered Prosopis juliflora, reflux it with a 10 % (v/v) methanol solution for 6 h, then filter the hot extract, let the filtrate stand overnight, and finally perform an aqueous extraction at 90 °C for 2 h before dissolving the residue in water at the required proportion to achieve a final concentration of 50 ppm P. juliflora extract in the concrete mixes.

steps.instruction: For each of the 16 mix designs listed in Table 3, weigh the specified amounts of cement, fly ash, metakaolin, fine aggregate, coarse aggregate, water (kg), super‑plasticizer (L) and add the P. juliflora extract to reach 50 ppm; mix thoroughly to obtain a homogeneous concrete batch.

steps.title: Cast test specimens
steps.instruction: From each concrete batch, cast the required specimen geometries for the different durability and mechanical tests:

substeps.instruction: For water absorption, RCPT, acid resistance, permeability, sorptivity, and UPV: cylinders or disks of 100 mm diameter and appropriate heights (50 mm thick for sorptivity, 100 mm × 200 mm for permeability, 50 mm thick for sorptivity, 50 mm thick × 100 mm diameter for RCPT).
For compressive strength: standard 150 mm cubes or 100 mm cylinders as per laboratory practice.

steps.title: Cure specimens
steps.instruction: Cover all freshly cast specimens with plastic sheets and store them in a curing room at 23 ± 2 °C and ≥95 % relative humidity for 28 days before any testing; thereafter keep them moist until the scheduled testing ages (7, 14, 28, 56, 90 days).

steps.title: Assess workability
steps.instruction: Immediately after mixing each batch, measure slump (mm) using a standard slump cone and compaction factor using the ASTM C 231 method; record values for each mix (e.g., T1 slump 107 mm, compaction factor 0.892, etc.).

steps.title: Determine compressive strength
steps.instruction: At 7, 14, 28, 56, and 90 days, test the designated cubes or cylinders in a compression testing machine at a loading rate of 0.25 MPa/s; record the maximum load and compute strength in MPa for each mix.

steps.title: Conduct saturated water absorption test
steps.instruction: Oven‑dry each specimen at 105 °C for 24 h, record dry weight (W₁), then submerge in water at room temperature for 24 h, surface‑dry, record saturated weight (W₂), and calculate absorption % = (W₂ − W₁)/W₁ × 100.

steps.title: Perform rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT)
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 mm thick, 100 mm diameter concrete disks, place each between two chambers—one filled with 0.3 N NaOH and the other with 3 % NaCl—apply 60 V DC for 6 h, then measure the total charge passed in Coulombs.

steps.title: Execute sulfuric acid resistance test (weight loss)
steps.instruction: After 28 days of curing, record initial weight (W₀) of each specimen, then immerse specimens in 5 % H₂SO₄ solution for 30 days; periodically remove, surface‑dry, weigh (W_t), and compute weight‑loss % = (W₀ − W_t)/W₀ × 100.

steps.title: Measure acid‑induced strength loss
steps.instruction: After the 30‑day acid exposure, test the specimens for compressive strength as described above and calculate strength‑loss % = (strength before – strength after)/strength before × 100.

steps.title: Carry out permeability test
steps.instruction: Place a 100 mm diameter × 200 mm height specimen in a permeability cell, apply water pressure incrementally from 0.5 MPa up to 1.5 MPa for a total duration of 24–72 h, then measure the penetration depth and compute permeability using Darcy’s law.

steps.title: Perform sorptivity test
steps.instruction: Oven‑dry a 100 mm diameter × 50 mm thick specimen, place its bottom surface in water 500 mm deep while sealing lateral sides, record weight at 5, 10, 30, 60 min, and calculate sorptivity S = I · t⁻⁰·⁵ (where I is cumulative water intake).

steps.title: Run ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) test
steps.instruction: Position transmitting and receiving transducers on opposite faces of each specimen, trigger a high‑frequency pulse, measure transit time (T), and compute velocity V = L/T (L = specimen thickness). Record V in m/s for each age.

steps.title: Compile and analyze results
steps.instruction: For each mix and curing age, tabulate slump, compaction factor, compressive strength, water absorption %, RCPT charge (Coulombs), acid‑weight loss %, acid‑strength loss %, permeability, sorptivity, and UPV; perform statistical analyses (ANOVA) as described to assess significance of differences.
